subject.title: [Bug]: Fallback model does not report progress correctly during long tasks

question: Should OpenClaw guarantee identical source-channel intermediate progress for long tasks across primary and fallback model candidates, including cross-provider fallbacks such as OpenAI to DeepSeek?
rationale: The source shows shared fallback and progress plumbing but no explicit product contract or live proof for provider-independent progress parity, and provider-specific streaming/tool-call behavior may make a hard guarantee costly or inaccurate.

options.title: Guarantee progress parity
options.body: Treat missing fallback progress as a core bug and require shared agent/channel tests plus live cross-provider proof before closing.

options.title: Document degraded fallback modes
options.body: Allow fallback providers to complete work with weaker intermediate progress when their stream/tool behavior differs, and document the limitation clearly.

options.title: Fold into broader fallback delivery semantics
options.body: Track this under a wider fallback delivery contract that also covers final-result routing, retry notices, and channel recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Guarantee progress parity
recommendation.body: Treat missing fallback progress as a core bug and require shared agent/channel tests plus live cross-provider proof before closing.

likelyOwner.reason: The fallback model feature history points to Peter Steinberger as the clearest available owner for the model fallback contract decision.
